why: The code edits are exact (schema.ts 289 and 7180 and the five register lines, which rg confirms are the only mentions), and the generated migration has a stop_if limiting it to two statements. But both migrations delete production data for good. The custom DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE relies on a hand-written guard over pg_constraint, pg_attribute, pg_views and pg_proc, and only its foreign-key branch is tested. A mistake in the view, column or function branch would let CASCADE drop objects outside commerce_legacy.
harm_if_wrong: CASCADE drops a view, column or function in another schema that depended on commerce_legacy, with only the dump as a way back.
make_it_cheaper: Add test cases for a dependent column type, a view and a function outside the schema, so every guard branch is checked.
brief_problems: The enum at schema.ts:289 spans several lines; the brief quotes it as one line ('the whole declaration' still makes the edit clear).
